chunks: A man struck another man on the head during the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. The injured man claimed that he could not see anything with his eyes, that he could not smell any scent, and that he had become mute and could not speak. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “If he is truthful, then three full blood-money compensations have become due to him.”

It was said to him: “How can that be determined from him, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, so that we may know he is truthful?” He said: “As for what he claims regarding his eyes, that he does not see with them, that is determined by telling him: ‘Raise your eyes toward the disc of the sun.’ If he is sound, he will be unable to refrain from closing his eyes; but if he is truthful, he will not see with them and his eyes will remain open. As for what he claims regarding his nostrils, that he does not smell any scent, that is determined by a burning substance brought near his nose. If he is sound, the smell of the burning substance will reach his brain, his eyes will water, and he will turn his head away. And as for what he claims regarding his tongue of muteness and that he does not speak, that is determined by a needle struck upon his tongue. If he speaks, the blood will come out red; and if he does not speak, the blood will come out black.”

key_terms.إِبْرَةٍ: a needle used here as a means of testing the claim
key_terms.الْحُرَاقِ: a burning or pungent substance used to test smell
key_terms.خَيَاشِيمِهِ: his nostrils, relating to the sense of smell
key_terms.دِيَاتِ: blood-money compensations due for bodily injury
key_terms.هَامَتِهِ: the head or skull, the place where the blow was struck
key_terms.يَسْتَبِينُ: is determined or made clear through examination

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali عليه السلام verify injury claims involving loss of sight, smell, and speech in legal cases?
ai.summary: This hadith records a judicial ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning bodily injury that allegedly caused loss of sight, smell, and speech. It outlines methods for verifying such claims and establishes that, if proven true, the victim is entitled to three blood-money compensations.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3250 - Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

A man struck another man on the head during the time of Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as). The injured man claimed that he could no longer see with his eyes, could not smell any fragrance, and had lost his speech, becoming mute.
Commander of the Faithful (as) said: "If he is truthful, then he is entitled to three blood-money compensations."

It was asked: "O Commander of the Faithful, how can it be verified whether he is truthful?"
Imam (as) replied: "As for what he claims about his eyes, that he cannot see, it can be verified by asking him to look up at the sun. If he is healthy, he will be unable to stop himself from closing his eyes, but if he is truthful and cannot see, his eyes will remain open.
As for his claim about his nose, that he cannot smell, it can be verified by bringing something pungent close to his nose. If he is healthy, the smell will reach his brain, his eyes will water, and he will turn his head away.
As for his claim about his tongue, that he is mute and cannot speak, it can be verified by pricking his tongue with a needle. If he is able to speak, the blood will flow red, but if he is mute, the blood will flow black."
